context.body: Gospel, Israel, and shared life · Romans 10:14–21
context.label: Gospel, Israel, and shared life

observations.body: Preaching, hearing, and resisted good news. How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? How will they believe in him whom they have not heard? How will they hear without a preacher? But about Israel he says, “All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.”

payload.posture: Read Romans 10:14–21 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states preaching, hearing, and resisted good news. How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? How will they believe in him whom they have not heard? How will they hear without a preacher? But about Israel he says, “All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.” It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
